title: Adwind_jRAT_Incident_Response_Scenario_2e9
description: Investigate and respond to a potential Adwind/jRAT compromise on a victim host.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The victim host in your network has exhibited unusual behavior, including unexpected network connections and suspicious process activity. Your task is to investigate and respond to this potential Adwind/jRAT compromise. Adwind/jRAT is a cross-platform Java-based Remote Access Trojan (RAT) known for its persistence mechanisms and data exfiltration capabilities.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter the word 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content:
You have SSH access to the victim host with the following credentials:
- Hostname: victim
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano

Enter the word 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Services
levels.content: Investigate the victim host for unauthorized or suspicious services. Enumerate running services and identify any that appear unauthorized or suspicious. Look for a suspicious service name.
levels.solution: To identify suspicious services, start by listing all active services and systemd timers. Use the command 'systemctl list-units --type=service --all' to list all services. Look for the service name 'network-diagnostics.service'.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Start by understanding the systemd service management system.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command 'systemctl list-units --type=service --all' to list all services.

levels.title: Identify Scheduled Tasks
levels.content: Determine if any scheduled tasks or timers are responsible for automatically executing suspicious processes. Identify scheduled execution persistence mechanisms that might be used to maintain malware activity. Look for a suspicious timer name.
levels.solution: To identify scheduled tasks, list all timers and filter for those that might trigger suspicious services or scripts. Use the command 'systemctl list-timers --all | grep network-diagnostics.timer' to specifically identify the timer name 'network-diagnostics.timer'.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Understand how systemd timers can be used to schedule tasks.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command 'systemctl list-timers --all | grep network-diagnostics.timer' to list all timers and filter for specific ones.

levels.title: Locate Malware Files
levels.content: Locate files installed by the malware on the compromised host. Correlate suspicious activity with files introduced by the trojan. Look for a suspicious file path.
levels.solution: To locate malware files, investigate unusual directories and files, especially those with recent modification times. Use the command 'ls -la /usr/local/bin/net-diag' to list the file. Look for the filename '/usr/local/bin/net-diag'.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Understand how malware often places files in unusual directories.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the command 'ls -la /usr/local/bin/net-diag' to investigate directories and files with recent modification times.
